explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation by comparing scores on the same test set using correlation metrics (Spearman and Pearson correlations) with normalized human adequacy scores

prompts.notes: Paper mentions using 5-shot prompts with demonstrations sampled from score intervals, following human annotation instructions. Two prompting templates are mentioned: one with error span detection followed by scoring, and one with direct scoring. Full templates are provided in figures but not reproduced in the main text.

guidelines.notes: Simplified MQM framework with error span detection (Addition, Omission, Mistranslation, Untranslated) and direct assessment (DA) scores 0-100 for adequacy. Same annotation protocol and tool as previous work referenced.

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on the entire SSA-MTE test set containing 12,768 examples across 11 language pairs that met quality thresholds

validation_results.summary_finding: Gemini 2.5 Pro achieves competitive correlations (Spearman: 0.633, Pearson: 0.667) with human judgments, though SSA-COMET-MTL performs slightly better on Pearson correlation and is more efficient for supported languages.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLMs were prompted to detect error spans in addition to scoring adequacy, but human evaluators provided more detailed error categorization. Both methods used adequacy scoring on 0-100 scale.
